title: Alert triage → incident response
description: Score alerts by user-visible impact, drop the ones no action follows from, and route the severe band to incident command with an explicit authorization gate.
yaml:
apiVersion: ladder.dev/v1alpha1
kind: Workflow
metadata:
  name: wf-sre-01
  title: Alert triage → incident response
  description: Score alerts by user-visible impact, drop the ones no action follows from, and route the
    severe band to incident command with an explicit authorization gate.
  version: 1.0.0
spec:
  objective: Turn an alert stream into a ranked response queue where every page corresponds to user-visible
    impact and severe events reach an incident commander immediately.
  policies:
    maxConcurrency: 4
    onFailure: preserve-completed
    requireApprovalFor:
      - n-approval
  nodes:
    - id: n-intake
      kind: input
      name: Alert stream and service context
      summary: Alert stream and service context
      inputSchema:
        type: object
        required:
          - text
        properties:
          text:
            type: string
            description: The requester's objective, source material, or instructions.
          workflowFields:
            type: object
            required:
              - alerts
              - slo_status
              - recent_changes
              - on_call_capacity
            properties:
              alerts: {}
              slo_status: {}
              recent_changes: {}
              on_call_capacity: {}
        x-ladder-input-mode: text
    - id: n-classify
      kind: agent
      templateRef: sre-05
      name: Score alerts by user-visible impact
      summary: Score and label every incoming item before anything is queued.
      role: Engineer building signals that answer questions rather than filling dashboards.
      prompt: You are an Observability Engineer. You define SLIs that reflect user-visible behavior, alerts
        that are actionable and tied to an owner, and instrumentation that answers the questions asked
        during a real incident. You remove alerts that fire without a corresponding action, because alert
        fatigue is a reliability risk with a measurable cost.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - observability
          - domain-analysis
          - operations-planning
          - incident-response
        tools:
          - read
          - write
        connectors:
          - mcp:observability
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
        required:
          - label
          - severity
          - confidence
          - rationale
        properties:
          label: {}
          severity: {}
          confidence: {}
          rationale: {}
    - id: n-filter
      kind: transform
      name: Drop out-of-scope items
      summary: keep alerts with an owner and a defined action, and drop those that consistently fire without
        one
      config:
        operation: filter
        expression: keep alerts with an owner and a defined action, and drop those that consistently fire
          without one
    - id: n-rank
      kind: transform
      name: Rank by urgency
      summary: sort by error_budget_burn_rate descending, then by affected_user_count descending
      config:
        operation: sort
        expression: sort by error_budget_burn_rate descending, then by affected_user_count descending
    - id: n-queue
      kind: transform
      name: Cut the actionable queue
      summary: take the first on_call_capacity alerts as the active queue
      config:
        operation: slice
        expression: take the first on_call_capacity alerts as the active queue
    - id: n-severity
      kind: condition
      name: Severity routing
      summary: Route on alert.severity selects one declared branch.
      config:
        expression: alert.severity selects one declared branch
        branches:
          - label: Escalate
            when: escalate
          - label: Standard
            when: standard
          - label: Default
            when: default
    - id: n-escalate
      kind: agent
      templateRef: sre-01
      name: Declare an incident and take command
      summary: Escalation path for the top band.
      role: Incident commander running response with clear roles and honest status.
      prompt: You are an Incident Commander. You establish impact, severity, and roles early, keep one
        authoritative status that internal and external audiences can both be given, and drive toward
        mitigation before diagnosis. You separate the mitigation decision from the root-cause debate,
        because incidents extend when the people who could stop the bleeding are arguing about why it
        started.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - incident-response
          - teaching
          - communication
          - domain-analysis
        tools:
          - read
          - write
        connectors:
          - mcp:pagerduty
          - mcp:slack
        permissions:
          - explicit-authorization-required
      outputSchema:
        type: object
    - id: n-handle
      kind: agent
      templateRef: sre-02
      name: Diagnose and mitigate within the on-call queue
      summary: Standard resolution path.
      role: Diagnostician isolating failure from telemetry under time pressure.
      prompt: You are a Reliability Diagnostician. You form hypotheses from metrics, logs, and traces,
        and you state the single observation that would eliminate each one so the investigation converges
        instead of wandering. You distinguish correlation in a deploy timeline from causation, because
        rolling back the wrong change extends the outage and destroys the evidence.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - observability
          - experiment-design
          - decision-analysis
          - domain-analysis
          - risk-analysis
        tools:
          - read
          - test
        connectors:
          - mcp:observability
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
    - id: n-rejoin
      kind: join
      name: Reconverge after routing
      summary: Release whichever routed path completed.
      config:
        join: first
    - id: n-approval
      kind: approval
      name: On-call lead authorizes mitigations that change production
      summary: Pause for the on-call lead; on timeout, escalate.
    - id: workflow-output
      kind: output
      name: Released deliverable
      summary: Return the completed Alert triage → incident response deliverable, the evidence behind
        it, and every unresolved item.
  edges:
    - id: wf-sre-01-edge-1
      from: n-intake
      to: n-classify
      kind: data
    - id: wf-sre-01-edge-2
      from: n-classify
      to: n-filter
      kind: data
    - id: wf-sre-01-edge-3
      from: n-filter
      to: n-rank
      kind: data
    - id: wf-sre-01-edge-4
      from: n-rank
      to: n-queue
      kind: data
    - id: wf-sre-01-edge-5
      from: n-queue
      to: n-severity
      kind: data
    - id: wf-sre-01-edge-6
      from: n-severity
      to: n-escalate
      kind: control
      condition: escalate
    - id: wf-sre-01-edge-7
      from: n-severity
      to: n-handle
      kind: control
      condition: standard
    - id: wf-sre-01-edge-8
      from: n-escalate
      to: n-rejoin
      kind: data
    - id: wf-sre-01-edge-9
      from: n-handle
      to: n-rejoin
      kind: data
    - id: wf-sre-01-edge-10
      from: n-rejoin
      to: n-approval
      kind: data
    - id: wf-sre-01-edge-11
      from: n-approval
      to: workflow-output
      kind: dependency
      condition: approved
